stops.note: pide's own pi extension (loaded with -e into every pi) registers ide_pin. execute() snaps start_line to the line containing `code`, refuses if it can't, and returns a result whose `details` is {pide: 1, kind: "pin", path, line, end_line, text, snippet, note}. That result is the only channel: there is no side socket.

pi emits tool_execution_end over RPC JSONL. The wire parser turns it into the usual ToolEnd event and, if the call didn't error, also runs collab_events on result.details, adding extra events after ToolEnd.
collab_event matches kind "pin" and builds a core collab::Pin. The id is the tool call id, and the anchor is the line plus that line's text, so the pin can be found again by its text later.

On the tokio side the connection reads each line, then resolve_collab_path makes the pin's relative path absolute against pi's cwd (canonicalized, so it matches workspace paths). It then sends the event over the inbound mpsc channel.
The UI-side cx.spawn loop takes each Inbound and applies it inside the session's Agent entity through handle_event.
Agent stores the pin in self.pins (replacing it in place if the id repeats), then calls persist_changes, which bumps notes_rev and saves it with the session. cx.notify() then wakes the observers.

stops.note: Each editor tab observes Sessions (watch_pi) and runs refresh_pi_marks when notified. It skips the work if no session's notes_rev changed. Otherwise it filters the agent's stops() to this file and re-finds each one with Anchor::locate against the current text.

Here the mark is drawn, entirely with GPUI Kit decorations: a gutter mark in colors::pi_note (other sessions' marks are dimmer), an overview-ruler mark in the scrollbar, and a faint tint on the note that's shown. render_pi_bar draws the note bar above the editor.

content.text: The tour has 8 stops. `ide_pin` in `ext/pide.ts` finds the line that contains the given code and returns its pin data in the tool result's `details`. pi sends that result as `tool_execution_end`, and `wire.rs` turns it into an `AgentEvent::Pin` (the line plus that line's text, so it can be found again). The connection makes its path absolute, and the session's `Agent` stores it and increases `notes_rev`. When that number changes, each open editor tab finds the pin's line again in its current text and draws it with GPUI Kit decorations: a mark in the gutter and the scrollbar, a tint on the lines, and a note bar above the editor.
